clue.text: Assured one friend in secret

blocks.note: assured and confident both mean sure of oneself
the Roman numeral for one
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone confides securely in a trusted pal, out of public earshot.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb phrase meaning privately, as when something is told with trust that it will not be passed on.

clue.text: Agreed and kept in touch

blocks.note: first meaning: matched or was consistent with
second meaning: exchanged letters with someone

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like two friends who agreed to stay in contact; the verb has both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to match or tally and to exchange letters, both in the past tense here.

clue.text: The things people write in bars!

definitions.text: The things people write in bars!

blocks.clueFragment: The things people write in bars!
blocks.note: surface reading: scribbles jotted down in pubs, perhaps on beer mats
setter's reading: bars are the measures of written music, filled with musical symbols

explanation.surface: Drinkers scribbling messages at the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars here are the divisions of a stave in sheet music, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers write musical symbols for pitch and duration inside each bar, and drinkers jot short messages too.

clue.text: Police officer reorganised PR section

indicators.note: something reorganised has been put into a new order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective shakes up the public-relations department.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in British police forces above sergeant, so a senior officer.

clue.text: Vehicle drivers

blocks.note: surface reading: the people who drive cars and lorries
setter's reading: the machines that power a vehicle and make it move

explanation.walkthrough: Drivers sounds like motorists, but it means the things that drive the vehicle along.
explanation.definitionFit: Motors are what propel cars and trains, literally driving them forward mechanically.

clue.text: Trade vehicles

blocks.note: first meaning: to deal or buy and sell, often illegally
second meaning: the cars and lorries moving on roads

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like commercial vans; the word means both dealing in goods and road vehicles collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dealing in goods, often illicit ones; as a noun it covers all road vehicles collectively.

clue.text: One 50 in years, yet nimble

indicators.note: in places the earlier items inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: an age is a long span of years
Roman numeral for one
Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A spry fifty-year-old, still light on their feet despite the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone able to move quickly and easily, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: One washing and ironing the continental strip

blocks.note: la is French for the, a continental language
to strip is to take one's clothes off

explanation.surface: A worker laundering a European team's football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip looks like a sports kit to be washed, but it is a verb meaning take clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to wash and press clothes and linen.

clue.text: Assesses artist before setback

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word before it from right to left

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
the front of this word is taken as written, the rest of it being the signal to turn it round

explanation.surface: A critic judges a painter after a disappointing setback.
explanation.walkthrough: Setback is split into two parts: set, then back as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to evaluate or judge its value, the same as assessing it.

clue.text: Kind Grace endlessly promises to pay

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Generous Grace keeps signing promises to settle her debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous and warm-hearted behaviour can be called either, so the adjectives are near synonyms.

clue.text: Mimic Tom, a prisoner being let out

indicators.note: a prisoner being let out is freed, so these letters are set loose to form a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict named Tom is released from jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer who copies other people's voices and mannerisms, so a mimic.

clue.text: Oriental church festival never ever overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is ignored, so the second word is removed from inside the first

blocks.note: the Christian festival of the Resurrection
taken as written
taken as written, then taken out of the previous word

explanation.surface: A spring religious holiday that has always been given its due.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the letters of ever from never leaves just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe things belonging to Asia and the lands lying to the east.

clue.text: One's not bound to enjoy it

definitions.text: One's not bound to enjoy it

blocks.clueFragment: One's not bound to enjoy it
blocks.note: surface reading: nobody is obliged to like something
setter's reading: someone not tied up or imprisoned enjoys this state

explanation.walkthrough: Bound reads as obliged, but it means tied up: those unshackled have this.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of being unrestrained, which is exactly what someone not tied up possesses.

clue.text: Factory scheme is on time

blocks.note: a plan is a scheme
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A works project is running on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial site where goods are manufactured, such as a car or chemical works.

clue.text: George wanted US car to fly!

blocks.note: auto is the American word for a car
to pilot a plane is to fly it

explanation.surface: A man called George longs for an American car that can take off.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old British airmen's slang for the automatic pilot, so the name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, a slang term still known in aviation.

clue.text: Take care, Giles! That could be blasphemy!

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning to a man named Giles that his words might offend the devout.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent treatment of something holy is the core meaning of both nouns, making them synonyms.

clue.text: I left note behind - a little one - being childish

indicators.note: behind sends the first three words' pieces after the phrase that follows them

blocks.note: an infant is a small child
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a message for a baby and is mocked as immature.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind tells you the first three pieces go after the little one.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour like a baby's or young child's is described by both adjectives, so they match.

clue.text: Their camp activities are uncovered

blocks.note: surface reading: some group's goings-on at a camp are exposed or revealed
setter's reading: people at this sort of camp do everything without clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Uncovered sounds like a scandal being exposed, but it simply means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists gather at camps where all activities are done without clothing, hence uncovered.

clue.text: As it can move like the devil!

indicators.note: if letters move they change places, giving a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Something dashing along as fast as possible, like the devil himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Like the devil looks like a speed idiom attached to move, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means characteristic of Satan, the devil, so devilish or evil.

clue.text: As ruler's involved, it's dreamlike

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's meddling in affairs has an unreal, fantastical quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and unreal like a dream, the quality associated with the art movement led by Dalí.

clue.text: Fellow takes advantage of electrical safety devices

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
to use someone is to take advantage of them

explanation.surface: A man exploits the circuit breakers in the house wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: These wire components melt when the current is too high, cutting the circuit to prevent fires.

clue.text: Former pilot's staggering feat

indicators.note: staggering means lurching unsteadily, so the letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: ex means former
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired aviator's astonishing achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: Staggering looks like praise for the feat, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold or daring deed is a feat, and that noun sense is shared by both.

clue.text: Removing top from platform causes hatred

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is to be taken away

blocks.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Taking the roof off a stage stirs up public anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread loathing or contempt directed at someone, a formal synonym for strong dislike.

clue.text: Rush to put away summary

blocks.note: to rush is to run
to down food or drink is to consume it quickly

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to tidy up a brief report.
explanation.walkthrough: Put away looks like storing, but here it means eating or drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief account of the main points is called a summary or an informal recap.

clue.text: A little hooter heard in the night

definitions.text: A little hooter heard in the night

blocks.clueFragment: A little hooter heard in the night
blocks.note: surface reading: a small car horn sounding after dark
setter's reading: a young bird that hoots, calling at night

explanation.walkthrough: Hooter suggests a horn or siren, but here it is the bird that hoots, and little makes it a young one.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby owl is a small nocturnal bird whose hooting call is heard after dark.

clue.text: Ian is in every single engineer's union

indicators.note: is in means the name sits inside the letters made by the other words

blocks.note: all means every single one
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A man called Ian belongs to a trade union for engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: Union looks like part of a trade-union picture, but it is the definition, meaning a joining together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact or association formed between parties for mutual benefit is a union.

clue.text: Home hired by mouth of creek

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a let property is one rented out

explanation.surface: A rented house standing where a stream meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of water running into the coast, often where a small stream enters.

clue.text: As hobbies go, one has things licked!

definitions.text: As hobbies go, one has things licked!

blocks.clueFragment: As hobbies go, one has things licked!
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who has mastered their pastime
setter's reading: the items in this collection are licked to stick them on letters

explanation.walkthrough: Has things licked means has mastered them, but here the items were literally licked, being gummed postage.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist collects postage items, which traditionally were moistened with the tongue before sticking on envelopes.
